title: Evaluation of Question Answering Systems: Complexity of judging a natural language
reasoning: The paper primarily focuses on the technical aspects of evaluating Question Answering (QA) systems, including algorithms, knowledge sources, question/answer types, benchmark datasets, and various quantitative evaluation scores. While it discusses human judgment and its inherent subjectivity/bias in evaluation, this is from a methodological standpoint (i.e., quantifying human judgment, reducing human error in annotation, and the limitations of metrics correlating with human scores), rather than directly evaluating QA systems on religion, morals, or ethics as a core component of the QA task or the evaluation criteria. It does not discuss model bias related to fairness, harmful content, or societal ethics.
